newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Implats says all refinery employees at work.
newsitem.headline: Implats says all refinery employees at work.

text.p: Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd (Implats) said on Friday all workers at its platinum refineries had reported for work despite the National Union of Mineworkers' notice of a formal strike on Thursday.
"At this stage all our employees have reported for work and there are no incidents of industrial unrest at the moment," Implats spokeswoman Marilyn Watson told Reuters.
Implats said on Thursday that the NUM had issued formal notification of a strike at Implats platinum refineries which would start on Friday.
Watson said Implats management remained committed to obtaining a negotiated settlement with the NUM.
The NUM could not immediately be reached for comment.

Implats said on Thursday its Refineries management and the union met on four occasions but settlement on annual wage increases could not be reached and the NUM declared a dispute which was referred to the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration.
Two further conciliation meetings were held after that but no settlement was achieved, Implats said.
Management's last wage offer was a 10.7 percent increase, the NUM's last offer was 19.2 percent.
Implats produced 499,000 ounces of refined platinum in the six months to end-December 1996.
